articles.title: Outcomes associated with suprapectoral versus subpectoral biceps tenodesis site after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair: a retrospective comparative cohort analysis.
articles.authors: Rosso C, Loske S, Audige L, Dao Trong ML, Weiss I, Mueller A, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary arthroscopic rotator cuff repair with biceps tenodesis
articles.outcomes: Range of motion, pain, strength, shoulder function scores, quality of life, groove pain, Popeye sign, and postoperative adverse events
articles.take_home: Both suprapectoral and subpectoral biceps tenodesis produced similar results for shoulder function and pain relief. The suprapectoral approach was more likely to result in a visible bulge in the arm (Popeye sign) after surgery, but showed a small strength advantage that was not clinically meaningful.

articles.title: The interaction of race and insurance type on length of stay and discharge disposition following reverse total shoulder arthroplasty: A statewide database study.
articles.authors: Morriss NJ, Jeong A, Shaikh HJ, Greif DN, Ramirez G, Thirukumaran C, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Length of stay and discharge disposition (home versus other)
articles.take_home: Black patients with commercial insurance had longer hospital stays and were less likely to go home after reverse shoulder replacement compared to White patients with the same insurance, suggesting some patients may face different care pathways after this operation.

articles.title: Proceedings from the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Orthopedic Infections: Prevention of Periprosthetic Shoulder Infection.
articles.authors: Namdari S, Zmistowski B, Fiandeiro M, Gupta S, Nicholson T
articles.study_type: International consensus meeting with systematic literature review
articles.population: International shoulder surgeons, infectious disease physicians, and microbiology experts
articles.outcomes: Consensus recommendations for preventing periprosthetic shoulder infection, including risk factors, perioperative management strategies, and identification of evidence gaps
articles.take_home: Experts agreed on several strategies to help prevent shoulder infection after surgery, such as avoiding steroid injections before surgery and using alcohol-based skin cleaning, but many questions lack strong evidence and more shoulder-specific research is needed.

articles.title: Anatomical Conoid Ligament Reconstruction Improves Posterior Stability in Neer Type IIB Distal Clavicle Fractures: A Cadaveric Biomechanical Study.
articles.authors: Kurata S, Inoue K, Tsujimura K, Imanaka A, Kawamura K, Sinthubua A, et al.
articles.population: Fresh-frozen cadaver shoulders with Neer type IIB distal clavicle fractures
articles.outcomes: Reduction accuracy (displacement rates in superior, anteroposterior and combined directions) and mechanical stability under superior and posterior loading
articles.take_home: Placing the surgical drill hole at the back of the clavicle (anatomical reconstruction) reduced backward movement better than placing it at the front, with a difference of 1.8 mm under backward loading. Both positions performed similarly for upward stability, though the clinical importance of this difference is not yet clear.

articles.title: Less Can Be as Effective as More: Two WOSI Items Capture Clinical Outcomes After Surgical Stabilization for Shoulder Instability.
articles.authors: Sawicka-Garbarek E, Kaszynski J, Cisowski P, Kaczmarek P, Slezak M, Soroko E, et al.
articles.study_type: Validation study of outcome measurement instrument
articles.population: Patients undergoing surgical stabilisation for shoulder instability
articles.outcomes: Association between psychological items of WOSI questionnaire (items 15 and 17 for function and range of motion; items 16 and 21 for pain) and overall patient-reported outcome measures including UCLA, Constant, ASES and SST scores
articles.take_home: Just two psychological questions from the WOSI questionnaire can capture how well patients are recovering after shoulder stabilisation surgery, potentially offering a simpler alternative to longer questionnaires. This psychological component was strongly linked to patients' pain, function and overall recovery.

articles.title: Proceedings from the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Orthopedic Infections: Diagnosis of Periprosthetic Shoulder Infection.
articles.authors: Namdari S, Zmistowski B, Fiandeiro M, Gupta S, Nicholson T
articles.study_type: International consensus meeting with modified Delphi process
articles.population: International shoulder surgeons, infectious disease physicians, and microbiology experts
articles.outcomes: Consensus recommendations for diagnosing shoulder prosthetic joint infection, including supported diagnostic measures (ESR, CRP, humeral component loosening, tissue biopsy, prolonged culture incubation) and unsupported measures (cloudy fluid, serum WBC, D-dimer, routine imaging)
articles.take_home: A new international consensus framework for diagnosing shoulder infections after shoulder replacement has been developed, recommending specific blood tests, tissue samples and culture methods whilst advising against routine use of certain imaging and blood tests. However, more research is needed as most recommendations are based on limited evidence.

articles.title: Platelet-Rich Plasma versus Corticosteroid Injections for Subacromial Impingement Syndrome: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Liu L, Roemer J, Gerges PE, Lugo E, John DQ, Lima DJL, et al.
articles.outcomes: Pain scores (VAS) and shoulder function (Constant score, UCLA scale) at short-term and mid-term follow-up
articles.take_home: Platelet-rich plasma injections and corticosteroid injections provided similar pain relief for shoulder impingement syndrome in the short to medium term, with no clear evidence that one is better than the other. Your choice between these treatments should consider cost, availability, and your own preferences.

articles.title: Factors Associated with Functional Improvement After Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty: A Comprehensive Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Xiong R, Li W, Wang S, Jiang C, Zhu Y
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Functional improvement measured by change in ASES score and Constant-Murley score from before to after surgery
articles.take_home: Patients who have had previous shoulder surgery tend to gain less functional improvement after reverse shoulder replacement. Cemented fixation of the upper arm bone and repair of the subscapularis muscle during surgery are associated with better functional outcomes.

articles.title: Liposomal bupivacaine-containing versus standard bupivacaine interscalene nerve blocks in shoulder surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Adan FO, Boeder M, Kent RN, Wethington MA, Wethington A, Comfort S, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing shoulder surgery receiving interscalene nerve blocks
articles.outcomes: Pain scores at 24 and 72 hours after surgery; opioid consumption at 24 and 72 hours
articles.take_home: Liposomal bupivacaine reduced pain scores slightly compared with standard bupivacaine, but the reduction was too small to matter in practice and did not reduce opioid use, so it may not be worth the extra cost.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of locking intramedullary nails versus locking plates for displaced proximal humeral fractures : a meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis of randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Alshayban MA, Mourad MA, Alasiri A, Alazzam AY, Alzahrani A
articles.study_type: Meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Adults with displaced proximal humeral fractures
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures at early (3 months), mid-term and long-term (≥24 months) follow-up including DASH score, Constant-Murley Score, American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, pain scores, reoperation rates and screw-related complications
articles.take_home: Locking intramedullary nails and locking plates produced similar results for shoulder fracture recovery in most cases. For the most complex fractures (three- and four-part breaks), locking plates showed a small advantage and lower rates of reoperation, though the difference was not large enough to be clinically important.

articles.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the Resisted Anterior Drawer (RAD) Test for Lateral Elbow Instability in Lateral Epicondylitis.
articles.outcomes: Sensitivity 95.8%, specificity 82.2%, overall accuracy 90.0% of the resisted anterior drawer test for detecting lateral elbow instability on MRI
articles.take_home: A simple clinical test called the resisted anterior drawer test can accurately detect lateral elbow instability in patients with lateral epicondylitis, with the amount of pain relief during the test correlating with the severity of instability seen on imaging.

articles.title: Forearm Pronation Mechanics and Prior Upper Extremity Injury History in Professional Baseball Pitchers: A Biomechanical Analysis.
articles.authors: Eskew J, Manzi J, Dowling B, Hingorani A, Mack V, Kew M, et al.
articles.outcomes: Forearm pronation mechanics (angle, velocity, excursion) and associations with prior upper extremity injuries including elbow injuries, ulnar collateral ligament sprains/tears, and SLAP/labral injuries
articles.take_home: Forearm pronation mechanics showed no significant link with most upper extremity injuries in pitchers, but pitchers with prior SLAP/labral shoulder injuries had reduced forearm pronation movement. This finding was exploratory and needs further research to confirm whether reduced pronation causes injury or results from it.

articles.title: Rotator Cuff Repair with Concomitant Biceps Tenodesis is Cost-Effective at Mid-Term Follow-up: A Systematic Review and Cost-Effective Analysis.
articles.authors: Berreta RS, Badin D, Koyejo LD, Chan D, Ashkar A, Siragusa J, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review and cost-effectiveness analysis using a decision tree economic model
articles.population: Patients with primary rotator cuff tears
articles.outcomes: Quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER), and net monetary benefit over 5 years
articles.take_home: Rotator cuff repair with biceps tenodesis costs more upfront but provides better quality of life over 5 years and represents good value for money compared to rotator cuff repair alone. The additional procedure was found to be cost-effective in about 9 out of 10 simulations.

articles.title: Revision arthroplasty is associated with significantly higher morbidity but not mortality compared with primary shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Morriss NJ, Manning JH, Prabhavalkar ON, Dussik CM, Mannava S
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using propensity score matching
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing revision or primary total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 7354 patients in each group after matching
articles.outcomes: Mortality, hospital admission, prosthetic joint infection, shoulder osteomyelitis, periprosthetic fracture, and repeat revision surgery at three months, one year, and three years
articles.take_home: Revision shoulder replacement surgery has more complications than primary surgery, including higher rates of infection and fracture. There was a slightly higher death rate in the first three months after revision surgery, but this difference did not continue beyond that timeframe.

articles.title: The Effect of EVOLVE Radial Head Arthroplasty Stem Tilt on Clinical Outcomes.
articles.authors: Tat J, Kheiran A, Grewal R, Athwal GS, Faber KJ, Drosdowech DS, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent smooth stem radial head arthroplasty for acute radial head fractures between 1999 and 2021
articles.outcomes: Clinical outcome scores (PREE, QuickDASH, MEPI), range of motion, complications, reoperations, and radiographic measurements including neck-shaft angle and implant alignment
articles.take_home: Patients whose radial head implant tilted excessively had worse functional outcome scores than those with normal alignment, though they did not have higher rates of complications or need for revision surgery. The excessive tilt tended to develop gradually over time rather than immediately after surgery.

articles.title: Pharmacological Inhibition of STING with H-151 Promotes Rotator Cuff Healing in Aged Rats.
articles.authors: Cai Z, Qu C, Hu J, Chen Z, Lu J, Wang W, et al.
articles.outcomes: Activation of cGAS-STING pathway, inflammaging markers, collagen organisation, cartilage regeneration, histological score, failure load, stiffness and tensile stress of repaired tendon-bone junction
articles.take_home: In aged rats, a drug called H-151 that blocks a pathway involved in ageing-related inflammation improved rotator cuff repair by reducing inflammation, improving collagen maturation and increasing the strength of the repaired tissue. This suggests STING-blocking drugs might help older patients recover better after rotator cuff surgery.

articles.title: A smaller preoperative-to-prosthetic center of rotation shift is associated with better range of motion after bony increased-offset reverse shoulder arthroplasty: A retrospective cohort study of 97 patients by the FP-UCBM Shoulder Group.
articles.authors: Ciuffreda M, Di Santo PL, De Rosa A, Franceschetti E, Paciotti M, Perricone G, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing bony increased-offset reverse shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Visual analog scale pain, Constant-Murley score, Simple Shoulder Test, active range of motion (abduction and forward flexion)
articles.take_home: Patients who had a smaller shift in the center of rotation from before to after surgery had slightly better shoulder movement, particularly in lifting the arm to the side and forward. However, the relationship was weak and the shift in centre of rotation should not be used as the main factor to predict how well surgery will work.

articles.title: Beyond scores: Predictable early recovery and independence after reverse shoulder arthroplasty for complex proximal humerus fractures.
articles.authors: Khan LAK, Yung E, Goyal D, Cairns DA, Kumar K, Barker S
articles.population: Patients aged 60 years and over with acute three- or four-part proximal humeral fractures or fracture-dislocations
articles.outcomes: Oxford Shoulder Score, range of motion, SF-12, patient satisfaction, time to independence in washing/dressing, household activities and driving, complication rate
articles.take_home: After reverse shoulder arthroplasty for complex upper arm bone fractures, older patients typically regained independence in washing and dressing within six weeks, returned to household activities and driving within eight to twelve weeks, and reported high satisfaction. The complication rate was low at 5.5%.

articles.title: Complete pectoralis major rupture with ipsilateral full-thickness supraspinatus tear following a wrestling injury.
articles.outcomes: Both pectoralis major and supraspinatus tears repaired surgically with return to gym training and sport
articles.take_home: A wrestling injury caused both a complete pectoralis major rupture and a full-thickness supraspinatus tear in the same shoulder, which were successfully repaired together. The visible chest injury could have masked the less obvious rotator cuff damage if imaging had not been done.
